method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse paraphrase of both formulations of completeness and both compactness arguments, direction checking for every entailment, derivability, consistency and satisfiability claim, and exact formula, macro, token, tag, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Introduction to completeness: semantic consequence versus derivability, consistent-set model existence, Hilbert's existence claim, compactness, direct model construction and the Löwenheim-Skolem consequence.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Completeness has two equivalent forms. Its first says that whenever a sentence A is a semantic consequence of sentences Gamma, a derivation also establishes Gamma proves A, so the proof system reaches every genuine consequence without exceeding it.
samples.checks: The entailment-to-derivability direction, sentence restrictions, Gamma/A roles and maximal-strength claim are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The second form says every consistent set of sentences is satisfiable. Hilbert held that noncontradictory axioms guarantee objects satisfying them, while Frege objected; model existence proves Hilbert correct in the limited sense that some structure or valuation makes all consistent axioms true.
samples.checks: Consistency remains proof-theoretic, satisfiability semantic, both FOL/propositional alternatives and the nested satisfaction formula are exact, and the translated quotation preserves its criterion-of-truth-and-existence claim.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A finite derivation uses only finitely many Gamma sentences. Completeness therefore yields compactness: every consequence already follows from a finite subset, equivalently a set is consistent if all its finite subsets are consistent.
samples.checks: The finiteness argument, consequence direction, subset scope and consistency equivalence are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The completeness construction turns a consistent sentence set into a satisfying structure and can instead begin with a finitely satisfiable set to prove compactness directly. In first-order logic it also yields a finite or denumerable model and illustrates the wider use of constructing structures from sentence sets.
samples.checks: Consistency and finite satisfiability remain distinct starting conditions; the FOL-only tag, finite/denumerable alternatives and Löwenheim-Skolem attribution are preserved.

source_observations: The historical quotation is translated as part of the frozen source and is not presented as independently checked archival wording.
The source's awkward phrase the proof of is rendered idiomatically as the proof while retaining the emphasis macro and the same mathematical claim.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, tags, identifiers and reference options match exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
संपूर्णता and संहतता remain the provisional logical-sense choices recorded in T110 and T181.
The historical quotation and attribution were reviewed only against the frozen English source, not an external primary document.
